You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report describes an overflow exception thrown when creating a Fraction from a double value very close to a simple fraction with a maxDenominator specified. From the code of the Fraction constructor taking a double and maxDenominator (line 141), it delegates to another private constructor with parameters (double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations).

In this private constructor (lines 178-243), the fraction is computed using a continued fraction algorithm that tries to approximate the double value with numerator/denominator pairs. It tracks overflow using a long "overflow" threshold set to Integer.MAX_VALUE.

The core iteration (lines 205-229) computes new numerator (p2) and denominator (q2) candidates, checking if either exceeds the overflow threshold. If so, it throws a FractionConversionException with the value and the fraction candidate that caused it.

The bug relates to the fact that when the next convergent causes either p2 or q2 to overflow past Integer.MAX_VALUE, an exception is thrown immediately (line 215) instead of returning the previous convergent. The code comment (line 214) acknowledges that this situation can happen when q2 may overflow in the next iteration if the last fraction was very close to the actual value, but currently it throws rather than returning the last valid fraction.

Hence, the exception happens when the value is very close to a simple fraction, but the continued fraction iteration is forced to overflow to get the perfect approximation, causing the constructor to throw.

The failing test calls new Fraction(0.5000000001, 10), a value close to 1/2 with max denominator 10. The code tries to find the best fraction with denominator <= 10 approximating the value, but in intermediate steps q2 or p2 can overflow leading to the exception.

This confirms the bug report: the constructor should avoid throwing an exception and instead return the last valid approximant if overflow would occur on the next step with a value very close to the input.

Recommended fix locations will be methods involved in the fraction construction and the exception throwing logic.

Next, I will identify which methods are best to fix this overflow handling.
org.apache.commons.math3.fraction.Fraction.Fraction(double,double,int,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
